claims.text: Interactions: digoxin = a P-gp substrate, so P-gp inhibitors/inducers Δ its levels;
claims.quote: Therefore, drugs that induce/inhibit P-glycoprotein have the potential to alter digoxin pharmacokinetics.

claims.text: amiodarone raises digoxin levels: halve the digoxin dose (or stop it) and watch for toxicity;
claims.quote: Increased digoxin concentration. Reduce digoxin by half or discontinue. If continued, monitor for evidence of toxicity.

claims.text: check a level b4 starting an interacting drug.
claims.quote: Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating concomitant drugs.

claims.text: Serum level: <0.5 ng/mL loses efficacy and >2 ng/mL adds toxicity w.o benefit;
claims.quote: Serum digoxin levels less than 0.5 ng/mL have been associated with diminished efficacy, while levels above 2 ng/mL have been associated with increased toxicity without increased benefit.
claims.locator: 2.5 Monitoring to Assess Safety, Efficacy, and Therapeutic Blood Levels

claims.text: draw just b4 the next dose or ≥6 h after the last dose,
claims.quote: Obtain serum digoxin concentrations just before the next scheduled LANOXIN dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose.
claims.locator: 2.5 Monitoring to Assess Safety, Efficacy, and Therapeutic Blood Levels

claims.text: and don't Δ the dose on one isolated level.
claims.quote: do not use an isolated measurement of serum digoxin concentration as the basis for increasing or decreasing the LANOXIN dose
claims.locator: 2.5 Monitoring to Assess Safety, Efficacy, and Therapeutic Blood Levels

claims.text: Toxicity: N/V, visual chgs and arrhythmias;
claims.quote: Indicated by nausea, vomiting, visual disturbances, and cardiac arrhythmias.

claims.text: ↔ VT, nonparoxysmal junctional tachy in AF and hyperkalemia are serious signs;
claims.quote: Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia, nonparoxysmal junctional tachycardia in the presence of atrial fibrillation, and hyperkalemia are serious signs of digitalis toxicity.

claims.text: hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia allows toxicity @ lower levels.
claims.quote: If hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia (often due to diuretic use) is present, lower doses and serum levels can still cause toxicity
discontinue LANOXIN and place the patient on a cardiac monitor
Correct hypokalemia by administering potassium so that serum potassium is maintained between 4.0 and 5.5 mmol/L.

claims.text: Digoxin Immune Fab for life-threatening arrhythmias or hyperkalemia;
claims.quote: Life threatening arrhythmias (ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, high degree A-V block, bradyarrhythma, sinus arrest) or hyperkalemia requires administration of Digoxin Immune Fab.
Bradycardia and heart block caused by digoxin are parasympathetically mediated and respond to atropine.
Digoxin is not effectively removed from the body by dialysis because of its large extravascular volume of distribution.

claims.text: Counsel: report N/V, persistent diarrhea, confusion, weakness or visual chgs (blurred or green-yellow vision, halos), which can mean the dose = too ↑.
claims.quote: Advise patients to contact their doctor or a health care professional if they experience nausea, vomiting, persistent diarrhea, confusion, weakness, or visual disturbances (including blurred vision, green-yellow color disturbances, halo effect) as these could be signs that the dose of LANOXIN may be too high.

claims.text: Verapamil can raise digoxin levels 50–75% in the first wk;
claims.quote: chronic verapamil treatment can increase serum digoxin levels by 50% to 75% during the first week of therapy

claims.text: monitor digoxin levels when starting, adjusting or stopping diltiazem.
